title: Grill round 2 — PR surfaces, the summary under the button, and dialog dismissal
summary:
Round 1 is complete: all 14 answers accepted, no skips. Four notes added requirements I can't turn into plan items without guessing. This round is **4 short questions**.

Your notes, quoted:

1. `branch-rows`: “btw, we're removing the one project/branch selection” — folded into the record as an acceptance criterion (the single Project picker and single Branch row are gone; the combined control replaces them).
2. `scope`: “issues, pr, resolve conflicts from the pr, new task, etc.” — Q1/Q2 below pin the exact surfaces and what selection means on the PR side.
3. `button-label`: “but keep listing the project and branch selected under that, like we have today” — Q3 below.
4. `apply-boundary`: “and avoid closing the modal/dialog when clicking outside” — Q4 below.

questions.title: Which task-creation surfaces must use the combined Select Projects control?
questions.why: Each surface is a separate wiring job, dirty-check rewrite and e2e file. The PR side is the ambiguous one because it has no project selector today.
questions.context: Your note named “issues, pr, resolve conflicts from the pr, new task, etc.” I found three existing task-creation surfaces: New Task, `CreateTaskFromIssueDialog` (“Work on this with Agetor” on an issue), and `ResolveConflictsDialog` (“Resolve with Agetor” on a conflicted PR, which renders only the locked Branch row). A PR “work on this” entry does **not** exist today. The CLI/TUI already take repeatable `--repo`; there is no visual picker to combine there.

evidence.label: PR opens straight from the GitHub dialog

options.label: New Task panel
options.description: The surface the task text names; already decided.
options.consequence: The baseline: button, per-project rows, forced Isolate.

options.label: Issue task dialog (“Work on this with Agetor”)
options.description: Shares `CreateTaskFromIssueDialog`; the issue's repo is locked first.
options.consequence: Same control as New Task; the issue repo cannot be unchecked, and the draft-dirty check must see every repo.

options.label: PR conflict dialog (“Resolve with Agetor”)
options.description: Today it has only a read-only Branch row; the PR fixes the repo and the head branch.
options.consequence: The combined control needs a locked-repo mode; a multi selection here is a new behaviour, not just a UI move.

options.label: A new “Work on this PR with Agetor” entry
options.description: Does not exist today; PRs only offer conflict resolution.
options.consequence: New feature: a PR task flow, its prompt, and its acceptance coverage; larger than this change.

recommendation.reason: The three existing task-creation surfaces; the PR entry would be a new feature rather than a consolidation of today's selectors.

questions.title: On the PR side, what may the combined control change?
questions.why: Conflict resolution is defined on one PR's head branch. Extra repositories would produce a multi-repo task where only one repo has PR context.
questions.context: The PR dialog creates a task with `existingBranch: context.headRef` on `context.path`; the server rejects `existingBranch` for a multi-repo create (`orchestrator.ts:12518-12519`). So “lock the PR's repo and add extras” is not just a UI choice — it would need a different branch story for the extras.

evidence.label: multi + existingBranch is rejected
evidence.code:
if (multiRepo && existingBranch) {
    return { error: "existingBranch isn't supported with multiple repositories — create the task on a fresh branch" };

evidence.label: PR head branch is the task branch
evidence.code:
"Resolve with Agetor" dialog for a PR's merge conflicts. Creates a task ON
the PR's head branch (`existingBranch: context.headRef`)

options.label: Show the PR's repo locked in the same control; no extra projects
options.description: The dialog has the same button/row language, but the repo and branch are fixed.
options.consequence: Visual consistency and no contract change; the button opens a selection with one locked row.

options.label: Lock the PR's repo first, allow extra repositories
options.consequence: The server rejects `existingBranch` for 2+; the PR repo would need a different branch story and the prompt/diff/PR surfaces need a story for the extras. Large.

options.label: Keep today's locked Branch row; no Select Projects on the PR side
options.description: The PR dialog does not adopt the control.
options.consequence: Least change; the combined control exists on New Task and the issue dialog only.

recommendation.reason: It honours “resolve conflicts from the PR” without inventing multi-repo conflict tasks the server cannot represent today.

questions.title: What does “keep listing the project and branch selected under that” mean on the form?
questions.why: Decides whether the form gains a second listing above the per-project rows, or the rows themselves are the listing.
questions.context: You chose `1 → project name; 2+ → “2 projects selected”`, and the layout is button → branch rows → Isolate. Each branch row already reads `Branch · <project>` and shows the selected ref in its trigger. A separate summary line would repeat the same project/ref pairs directly above the rows.

evidence.label: the row that would be the listing

options.label: The per-project rows are the listing; no extra summary line
options.description: Button label, then one `Branch · <project>` row per selected project.
options.consequence: No duplicate information; the row label must always name the project (which Q11 of round 1 already requires).

options.label: Add a compact summary line under the button, above the rows
options.description: One line per project: name plus its selected branch.
options.consequence: A second listing to keep in sync with the rows; the form grows by N lines.

options.label: Keep the current 2+ summary card (project names) under the button, plus the rows
options.description: The existing names-only card survives above the per-project rows.
options.consequence: Keeps a familiar block, but it duplicates the row labels and still does not show branches.

recommendation.reason: The rows already show exactly the project + branch pair; a summary line would repeat it and drift when a ref changes.

questions.title: Outside click is ignored — what about Escape, and which dialogs does that cover?
questions.why: The shared `Dialog` closes on both backdrop click and Escape. Changing it for one caller needs a scoped prop; changing it for all task dialogs changes every modal's manners.
questions.context: The shared primitive documents “Escape and backdrop click invoke `onClose`” and implements both (`dialog.tsx:57`, `:108`, `:211`). The issue and PR dialogs use the same primitive. Your note was on the Select Projects dialog, so the rule can be scoped to it or applied to every task-creation dialog.

evidence.label: documented behaviour
evidence.code: *  - Escape and backdrop click invoke `onClose`. `onClose` is captured into a

options.label: Select Projects only: outside click ignored; Escape and Cancel still close
options.consequence: One scoped `closeOnBackdrop={false}`; keyboard exit remains, so the dialog is never trapped.

options.label: Select Projects only: outside click and Escape ignored; only Cancel/Save close
options.consequence: Protects an in-progress selection hardest, but removes the keyboard exit and can feel stuck.

options.label: All task-creation dialogs: outside click ignored; Escape and Cancel still close
options.consequence: Consistent across New Task, issue and PR dialogs; every backdrop-click close in those flows changes.

options.label: All task-creation dialogs: outside click and Escape ignored; only Cancel/Save close
options.consequence: Most protective and most intrusive; a user without a mouse has only the buttons.

recommendation.reason: The note was about the new selection dialog; keeping Escape preserves a keyboard exit and avoids changing every other modal.
